rationale: Both use the same structure: mutex-protected counters, and an embedded read counter and write counter for the combined type. A only adds n to the byte total when err == nil. That breaks the io.Reader and io.Writer contract, under which a call can return n > 0 together with an error, for example data plus io.EOF or a short write. A would under-count bytes that really moved, which matters for a billing wrapper. B always adds n, which is correct. A's doc comments and its clearer field name (bytes rather than n) are pluses, and B lays each type out next to its constructor and methods, which reads well. B's correct handling of partial reads and writes is the deciding factor.
